messages:
jess: heads-up — running into TS inference loss when using the SDK in an Edge build (Cloudflare) + ESM. Generic on client.chat.completions<T>() ends up as unknown.
jess: quick repro: SDK v1.0.6, TS 5.3, esbuild via wrangler. tsconfig uses moduleResolution: bundler and declaration: true.
jess: tsconfig snippet:
```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "module": "ESNext",
    "moduleResolution": "bundler",
    "declaration": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true
  }
}
```
jess: usage:
```ts
import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference'
const c = createClient({ apiKey: '' })
const r = await c.chat.completions<{meta:{score:number}}>(/*...*/)
// editor shows r as unknown-ish, no inference on meta.score
```
omar: thanks. we've seen this — bundler resolution picks the per-entrypoint .d.ts (esm/cjs) and our overloads were emitted separately which confuses inference. quick workarounds: set moduleResolution to nodeNext/node16 OR enable esModuleInterop and use default import form (import createClient from '@redwood/inference').
jess: tried nodeNext — fixed in editor. Not ideal to force that on users though.
omar: long-term: we'll consolidate overloads into a single exported interface and ship a canonical dist/types/index.d.ts so bundlers don't accidentally pick a partial signature. I'll open a small, types-only PR.
typebot: issue opened: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/501 — "Edge ESM: generic inference lost due to split declaration overloads"
omar: also adding a short note in the README under "Edge/ESM gotchas" with the two workarounds and an example Vite/esbuild config.
jess: excellent — thanks. Saved me debugging time. For now I pegged moduleResolution=nodeNext in our Pages build.
build-bot: types-only CI for branch/types/ems-typing-shim queued
